title: Focus & Elevation System for High-Contrast Inverted Brand Palettes
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a cohesive focus and elevation token system for 'inverted' brand palettes (dark UIs that preserve brand hue) with the following goals: 1) keep interactive focus states and elevation cues legible at typical console densities, 2) allow per-customer brand accents to surface without breaking contrast or UX hierarchy, 3) provide a clear mapping strategy so engineering can implement deterministic fallbacks and runtime adjustments for on-prem / Dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Semantic focus token set defined and documented (focus-outline, focus-ring-offset, focus-visible threshold)
Elevation tokens for dense and roomy densities (e.g., z-elevation-0..5) with color/outline variants for inverted palettes
Contrast checks: all interactive states meet WCAG 2.1 AA for 3:1 where required and 4.5:1 for primary CTAs in default console scale
Component overrides documented for Buttons, Table rows, and Chart interaction highlights with real examples in Storybook
A minimal runtime mapping approach documented for engineering: build-time semantic tokens + runtime brand delta adjustments
Design spec and Figma components published; linkage to PR and Storybook examples included
decisions: Adopt three-layer token strategy: 1) semantic core tokens (surface, text, interactive, border), 2) computed palette tokens (derived from brand hue + inversion rules), 3) component overrides for dense/legacy controls
Prefer build-time derivation of computed tokens with a small runtime delta API to avoid layout jank in low-spec Private deployments
Use a constrained brand-saturation clamp when deriving inverted accents to prevent low-contrast brand variants (max chroma reduction of 30%)
Expose focus visibility as an opt-in runtime flag for customers who require brand-faithful visuals in air-gapped installs (default preserves accessibility)
tradeoffs: Runtime-only brand mapping gives most flexibility for customers but increases runtime complexity; we chose build-time derivation + small runtime adjustments to balance predictability and flexibility
Clamping brand saturation protects contrast but may reduce perceived brand vibrancy for some customers; documented trade-off and opt-in override available
Component-level overrides increase bundle size and implementation surface area but are necessary for legacy dense tables and charts where semantic tokens alone are insufficient
implementation_notes: Engineering request: provide token JSON export (flat key: value) and SCSS/CSS var mappings. See example payload in Confluence page
Charts: prefer stroke + subtle glow approach over heavy shadows for inverted charts to avoid haloing on black backgrounds
Tables: row hover must use overlay blend with alpha overlay rather than saturating brand accent to maintain legibility on mixed-brand rows
Buttons: primary filled CTA should maintain 4.5:1 contrast on dark surface; provide outline variant for extremely saturated brand colors
